title: WASI components, HTTP MCP and scalable execution
claim_boundary: Source-verified implementation only; higher evidence levels require the named open gates. Path presence is not behavioural proof; assertion-level traceability governs implementation claims.

assertions.statement: Implement WIT host/guest SDK and signed manifest verification
open_gates: Compile the WIT host/guest boundary and run a component conformance suite under the reviewed runtime sandbox.
Establish accountable publisher identity, protected key custody, registry distribution, transparency and observed revocation propagation evidence.
assertions.permitted_claim: Exact provider-component bytes, manifest identity, bounded Ed25519 key authority, validity windows and reviewed revocations are compiler-tested locally; publisher identity, distribution, runtime sandboxing and live provider support remain unproven.

open_gates: Compile WASI components and run the component conformance suite.
Implement and compile the WIT host/guest boundary with Wasmtime resource controls.
assertions.permitted_claim: Execution envelopes, host network allowlisting, and component capability authorization are compiler-tested; live Wasmtime runtime fuel limits, memory limits, and guest capability enforcement remain uncompiled.

assertions.statement: Add Arrow/Parquet/DuckDB feature for large corpora
open_gates: Implement Arrow, Parquet and DuckDB large-corpus storage and query paths.
Execute large corpus performance and memory benchmarks on >1M study reviews.
assertions.permitted_claim: StudyGraph and review store contracts validate corpus structures; columnar Arrow, Parquet and DuckDB query engines remain unintegrated pending scalable execution benchmarks.

open_gates: Implement authenticated Streamable HTTP advanced capabilities only after Track 34 binds principal, tenant, region, scope, approval, quotas and audit state.
Execute remote or distributed overload, disconnect, chaos, failover and production-cache tests before scalable execution claims.
assertions.permitted_claim: Official rmcp clients verify bounded local-stdio prompt completion, current-only non-authoritative form elicitation, pagination, task completion and cancellation, four-slot admission recovery, and genuine aggregate task-activity notifications; approval authority, durable Tasks, production caching, stress/load performance, remote and scalable execution are denied.

assertions.statement: Add OAuth, tenancy, quotas, observability and deployment threat model
open_gates: Implement and threat-model authenticated Streamable HTTP/OAuth transport.
Implement authenticated Streamable HTTP advanced capabilities only after Track 34 binds principal, tenant, region, scope, approval, quotas and audit state.
assertions.permitted_claim: Candidate HTTP OpenAPI routes and local MCP listener bindings are defined; authenticated Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0 proxy tokens, multi-tenant isolation, and deployment threat models remain unproven.

open_gates: Compile and exercise WASI cancellation and compatibility paths.
Execute remote overload, disconnect and cancellation recovery after Track 34 authority controls.
assertions.permitted_claim: Local current and previous MCP profiles are compiler-tested; current local Tasks prove deterministic four-slot admission, fifth-request rejection, completion, cancellation and post-cancellation recovery. This is not load or scalability proof; WASI and remote cancellation, overload, chaos or failover recovery are not proven.
